[Question] How has coming out of long-time early access period affected the popularity of some of the more popular ex-early access games?

Normally if out of early access means "no more content updates", it starts to lose popularity.

Nobody knows when a game comes out of early access (aka it launches) whether there will be future content updates or not. Progressing through development in the early access programme to a successful polished launch is always a positive thing. The reason we don't see it that often is because the program hasn't been around long enough yet.

Any time you can show a successful outcome from the early access programme, it's going to have a positive outcome for the games who were successful. Whether or not the devs plan to continue adding content after the fact is largely irrelevant.
